assets.name: Parade Animal Cards
assets.purpose: Reusable physical cards used by pairs to build, manipulate, read, and translate parade patterns. The core manipulative of the entire unit — used in every lesson by every pair.
assets.page_layout: Two letter pages, portrait orientation, each holding 8 cards in a 2x4 grid. Each card is approximately 3in × 3in with thin solid cut-lines between cards. The 16-card set contains 4 of each animal: Bea (red vest), Finn (blue vest), Bibi (green vest), Moss (yellow vest). Page 1 holds 4 Bea + 4 Finn cards; page 2 holds 4 Bibi + 4 Moss cards (so a teacher only printing AB-pattern lessons can print page 1 only).

image_placeholders.description: A 3in × 3in square B&W line-art card showing Bea the Bear in cartoon style: simple bold outlines, brown fur indicated by short hatching, friendly smile, wearing a small vest filled with a SOLID dark pattern (so Bea is visually distinct from the other animals' vests in B&W). Centred on the card with a thin black border. The animal fills about 80% of the card. Same stroke weight and proportions as Finn, Bibi, and Moss.
image_placeholders.placement: Repeated 4 times in a 2x2 portion of page 1.

image_placeholders.description: A 3in × 3in square B&W line-art card showing Finn the Fox in matching style: simple bold outlines, friendly smile, wearing a small vest filled with HORIZONTAL STRIPES (so Finn's vest is visually distinct from the other animals in B&W). Centred, thin black border. Identical stroke weight to Bea, Bibi, Moss.
image_placeholders.placement: Repeated 4 times in a 2x2 portion of page 1.

image_placeholders.description: A 3in × 3in square B&W line-art card showing Bibi the Beaver in matching style: simple bold outlines, paddle tail visible, friendly smile, wearing a small vest filled with DOTS / POLKA-DOT pattern (so Bibi's vest is visually distinct from the other animals in B&W). Centred, thin black border. Same stroke weight.
image_placeholders.placement: Repeated 4 times in a 2x2 portion of page 2.

image_placeholders.description: A 3in × 3in square B&W line-art card showing Moss the Moose in matching style: simple bold outlines, small antlers, friendly smile, wearing a small vest filled with a CHECKERED / GRID pattern (so Moss's vest is visually distinct from the other animals in B&W). Centred, thin black border. Same stroke weight.
image_placeholders.placement: Repeated 4 times in a 2x2 portion of page 2.

teacher_prep_steps: Print both pages (one set per pair — for a class of 20 print 10 sets = 20 pages).
Optional but strongly recommended: laminate before cutting, so the cards survive K hands across multiple lessons.
Cut along the thin solid lines into 16 individual 3in × 3in cards per set.
Store each set in a labelled zip-top bag or envelope ('Parade Animal Cards — Pair 1', etc.).

Optional colour suggestion: if you have a colour printer and the budget for it, you may colour-print so each animal's vest is its named colour (Bea = red, Finn = blue, Bibi = green, Moss = yellow). The unit works equally well in B&W because each vest also has a unique pattern fill (solid, stripes, dots, checkered) that distinguishes the four animals visually.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 set (16 cards) per pair = 10 sets for a class of 20 students.

assets.name: Blank Parade Strip
assets.purpose: A printable strip with 5 cells that pairs use to lay out animal cards, build patterns, and visualize the parade route. The teacher also uses larger versions of the same strip during whole-group circle time for whole-class demonstrations.
assets.page_layout: Letter page, landscape orientation, with 2 horizontal parade strips stacked (one above, one below). Each strip is 5 cells wide, each cell ~1.5in square, with footprint icons drawn faintly beneath. A thin solid cut-line separates the two strips.

image_placeholders.description: A horizontal 5-cell parade strip in B&W line-art style. Each cell is approximately 1.5in × 1.5in with a solid light-grey border, sized to hold a 1.4in animal card or sticker comfortably. Below the cells, faintly drawn footprints suggest a parade route from left to right. The whole strip is approximately 8in wide × 2in tall. Identical to the strip layout used in the worksheets so children recognize it immediately.
image_placeholders.placement: Printed twice per page (top half and bottom half), separated by a thin solid cut line.

teacher_prep_steps: Print enough pages to yield ~12 strips (one per pair plus 2 spare = 6 pages, since each page produces 2 strips).
Laminate the pages — this lets pairs use dry-erase markers if they want to draw on the strips later, and protects against snack crumbs.
Cut along the horizontal cut line between the two strips on each page.
Distribute one strip per pair; keep 2 extras at the teacher table for whole-group demonstrations.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 strip per pair plus 2 spare for the teacher's whole-group demos = 12 strips total for a class of 20.

assets.name: Sound and Movement Cards
assets.purpose: An 8-card set used by the class and by pairs to translate visual patterns into auditory and kinesthetic patterns. Used in Lesson 3 (Same Beat, Different Parade) and Lesson 5 (summative, optional).
assets.page_layout: One letter page, portrait orientation, with 8 cards in a 2x4 grid. Each card is approximately 3in × 3in. Cards depict: clap (open hand), stomp (footprint), jump (jumping figure), freeze (hand up, palm out), hum (musical note + lips), tap (finger on surface), wave (waving hand), spin (circular arrow). Thin solid cut-lines between cards.

image_placeholders.description: A 3in × 3in card showing two open hands meeting — the universal clap icon. Simple, bold B&W line art, child-friendly. Word 'CLAP' printed beneath the icon in clear K-readable type.
A 3in × 3in card showing a single footprint pressed firmly into the ground — the stomp icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'STOMP' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing a stick figure with arms up and feet off the ground — the jump icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'JUMP' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing a stick figure standing perfectly still with one hand up, palm facing out — the freeze icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'FREEZE' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing closed lips with a small musical note hovering above — the hum icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'HUM' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing a single finger lightly tapping a surface, with two small motion lines — the tap icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'TAP' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing an open hand mid-wave with two small motion lines — the wave icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'WAVE' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing a circular arrow indicating rotation — the spin icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'SPIN' printed beneath.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 1 page (the teacher only needs one class set; not one per pair).
Laminate the page for durability.
Cut along the cut-lines into 8 individual cards.
Store the set in a labelled envelope. Bring to circle time for Lesson 3 and Lesson 5.
Optional colour suggestion: B&W works well; print in colour only if you specifically want extra visual variety for whole-group circle time.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 class set (8 cards) — used by the teacher in circle time, not distributed to pairs.

assets.name: Missing Mystery Card
assets.purpose: A small card showing a question mark inside a dotted outline. Placed in a parade strip to indicate that an animal is missing from that position. Used heavily in Lesson 4 (Fix the Broken Parade) and available in Lesson 5 for challenge mode.
assets.page_layout: One letter page, portrait orientation, with 12 cards in a 3x4 grid. Each card is approximately 2in × 2in (smaller than the animal cards so it visually 'belongs' inside an empty cell). Identical design on every card.

image_placeholders.description: A 2in × 2in square card with a thin solid border. Inside, a dashed-outline rectangle filling about 80% of the card. Inside that dashed rectangle, a large bold question mark (~1in tall) drawn in dark grey or black. Simple, instantly recognizable to a Kindergartener as 'something is missing here'. Identical on every card on the page.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 1 page (12 cards is enough for a class of 20 — 5 cards per pair × 10 pairs = 50, so print 4–5 pages).
Laminate before cutting.
Cut along the cut-lines into individual 2in × 2in cards.
Distribute 5 cards per pair before Lesson 4.
assets.quantity_per_class: 5 cards per pair = 50 cards = 4–5 printed pages for a class of 20.

assets.name: Core Loop Frame
assets.purpose: A reusable physical frame that students place over the repeating part of a parade strip to mark and isolate the core. Used in Lesson 2 (introduction of 'core'), Lesson 3 (verifying same-core-different-rep), Lesson 4 (using the core to fix gaps), and Lesson 5 (summative).
assets.page_layout: One letter page, portrait orientation, with 4 oval/lasso frames in a 2x2 grid. Each oval is approximately 4in wide × 1.7in tall, designed to frame a 2-, 3-, or sometimes 4-cell core comfortably. Each oval has a thin solid outer line and a thicker inner-edge line for visual emphasis. Cut-lines around each oval.

image_placeholders.description: A horizontal oval frame approximately 4in wide × 1.7in tall, drawn as a thick black outline (about 4pt) on a white interior. The shape is a clean ellipse — wide and short, so it can be placed over 2 or 3 cells of a parade strip without occluding the animal icons inside. No fill, no shadow, no decoration — just the frame outline. The same shape is sometimes called a 'lasso' in the teacher script.
image_placeholders.placement: Repeated 4 times in a 2x2 grid on the page.

teacher_prep_steps: Print on cardstock if available — durability matters because pairs handle these repeatedly.
Alternative: print on regular paper and laminate.
Cut around the outside of each oval to produce 4 frames per page (3 pages = 12 frames for a class of 20 = ~1 per pair plus spares).
Distribute one frame per pair before Lesson 2.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 frame per pair plus 2 spares = 12 frames = 3 pages for a class of 20.

assets.name: Coco the Conductor Puppet
assets.purpose: A printable Coco illustration that the teacher mounts on a popsicle stick to use as a recurring class character throughout all 5 lessons. Coco hosts each circle time, holds up the parade strips, and is the friendly face of the unit.
assets.page_layout: One letter page, portrait orientation, with a single large Coco illustration (~7in tall) and a small rectangular tab (~1in × 3in) at the bottom for the popsicle stick to be glued or taped behind. A thin cut-line traces the outside of Coco's silhouette including the tab.

image_placeholders.description: A full-body B&W line-art cartoon illustration of Coco the Conductor, approximately 7in tall: a friendly parrot with bold simple outlines, feather details indicated with line-art hatching (no fill), big round eyes, a warm smile, holding a small wooden conductor's baton in one wing. Slightly stylized, Kindergarten-appropriate, no scary or sharp features. At the bottom of the illustration, a small rectangular tab (~1in × 3in) extends below Coco's feet — this is for gluing the popsicle stick behind. A thin cut-line traces the outside of Coco's body including the tab. References blueprint.recurring_characters['Coco the Conductor'].visual_description; the colour version (red and yellow feathers) is achievable by colouring in the B&W line art.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 1 page on cardstock if possible (or regular paper + laminate for durability).
Cut around the outside of Coco's silhouette including the bottom tab.
Glue or tape a popsicle stick or tongue depressor behind the bottom tab so Coco can be held up like a puppet.
Optional: laminate before cutting for years of reuse.
Store flat in a folder so the puppet doesn't crease.

Optional colour suggestion: the design is intentionally B&W line art so any printer can produce it. If you have a colour printer, print in colour. Alternatively — and this is a lovely Day-0 activity — give children the B&W Coco and have them colour it together as a class before Lesson 1, with red and yellow feathers as the canonical palette.

assets.name: Anchor Chart Word Cards
assets.purpose: A printable set of four word cards (PATTERN, CORE, MISSING, EXTEND) with child-voice definitions and small visual cues. The teacher tapes each card to the class anchor chart as the corresponding word is introduced across the unit, replacing hand-printed words with a reusable, legible artifact.
assets.page_layout: One letter page, portrait orientation, with 4 word cards in a 2x2 grid. Each card is approximately 3.5in × 4.5in. Each card has the WORD in large bold uppercase at the top, the child-voice definition underneath in smaller K-readable type, and a small visual cue icon (a clap-stomp pair, a core loop, a question mark, or an arrow) in the corner. Thin solid cut-lines between cards.

image_placeholders.description: A 3.5in × 4.5in word card. Large bold uppercase 'PATTERN' centred at the top (~1.2in tall lettering). Below the word, in clear K-readable type (~0.4in tall): 'Something that repeats in the same order.' In the lower-right corner, a small clap-stomp icon pair (~0.8in tall) — open hand next to a footprint — to visually anchor the term. Thin black border around the card. B&W line art only.

A 3.5in × 4.5in word card. Large bold uppercase 'CORE' centred at the top. Below: 'The little part of the pattern that keeps repeating.' Lower-right corner: a small Core Loop Frame icon (~0.8in tall) — the lasso/oval shape — matching the M5 manipulative. Thin black border. B&W line art only.

A 3.5in × 4.5in word card. Large bold uppercase 'MISSING' centred at the top. Below: 'A part of the pattern that is not there yet.' Lower-right corner: a small question-mark-in-dashed-box icon (~0.8in tall) matching the M4 Missing Mystery Card design. Thin black border. B&W line art only.

A 3.5in × 4.5in word card. Large bold uppercase 'EXTEND' centred at the top. Below: 'To keep the pattern going.' Lower-right corner: a small bidirectional arrow icon (~0.8in tall) — a left arrow and a right arrow joined, representing extension in both directions. Thin black border. B&W line art only.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 1 page (1 set per class is enough — these go on the wall, not in pair bags).
Laminate the page for durability before cutting; this set will last for next year's class too.
Cut along the cut-lines into 4 individual word cards.
On Day 1, after introducing 'pattern', tape the PATTERN card to your anchor chart paper.
On Day 2, after introducing 'core', tape the CORE card below PATTERN.
On Day 4, after introducing 'missing' and 'extend', tape both MISSING and EXTEND cards.
Save the laminated set in a folder labelled 'Pattern Parade — Anchor Words' for re-use next year.

overall_prep_notes: Total prep time across all 7 assets: approximately 90 minutes for a class of 20. Default print spec is BLACK AND WHITE for every asset — this ensures any printer in any classroom can produce the unit. Colour printing is suggested in several assets (M1, M3, Coco) for visual richness only; the unit works equally well in B&W because animal vests use distinct pattern fills (solid / stripes / dots / checkered) and Coco is line art that children can colour as a Day-0 activity. Recommended prep approach: prep the entire unit's manipulatives in one sitting before Lesson 1 — front-loads the work but means the unit runs smoothly day-to-day. Alternative: prep M1 + M2 + M6 + Coco before Lesson 1 (~55 min), then prep M5 the night before Lesson 2, M3 before Lesson 3, and M4 before Lesson 4. Storage: keep all sets in a labelled bin or shelf, with each pair's set in its own bag. The animal cards (M1) are by far the most-used asset — laminate these even if you skip lamination on others.
